items.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Cecil McBee; the interviewer quotes McBee to ask a question.

ctx.x: Yes. I had a question that had to do with spirituality. And I think I’m guilty of for too long when people bring up spirituality I think of religion or faith. And I wanted to read something that Cecil McBee said in a conversation I had with him last November. And it was about spirituality and different periods in jazz. And he said, “well if it ain’t spiritual don’t play it. You know your spirit is what makes you play the instrument. If you’re not spiritual you ain’t feeling nothing. Elvin Jones used to say, ‘if…

Oh yeah. I basically want to have a spiritual connection to the musicians that I’m performing with at the time and so I have their capabilities in mind. Sometimes when I’m writing something I says well so-and-so-and-so would probably like to solo off this or play this you know. So there is that spiritual connection to your fellow musicians you know, a lot when you’re writing songs you know if you are looking for some sort of inspiration. And my inspiration generally is rhythmical, dealing with the drums you know.…
